circumstance.context: Tess's Proposal: Chat Widget on a Web Form

segments.exact: Two prior corrections in the perspective already walked the "SMS is the product" framing back from its strongest form — the SMS-first product is an overstatement, it's an open product idea, and the consumer motion is gated on understanding usage patterns and cost-per-behavior.

circumstance.context: Narrowing the SMS Framing, Not Killing It

segments.exact: Today's insight narrows it further.

circumstance.context: Narrowing the SMS Framing, Not Killing It

segments.exact: SMS remains viable for high-trust, post-consent, consumer-viral contexts — the channel works where the sender is already welcome.

circumstance.context: Narrowing the SMS Framing, Not Killing It

segments.exact: A chat widget on the share page is the right fit for evaluator, skeptic, first-touch, and demo contexts — no number, no verification, no opt-in form, no spam frame.
